question.text: Kaveri Growth Fund is at the end of year 5 of a 7-year tenure. The Manager is planning the 'Harvest Returns' phase. Which of the following BEST captures the Manager's focus in this phase?

answer.text: Aggressively raising the successor fund to replace LP commitments.
Deploying remaining dry powder into new investments regardless of market cycle.

Understanding industry and market cycles, managing exit risks and appropriately realising returns from investments — since harvesting returns by managing exit risks is 'probably the most important skill of an investment manager' for illiquid AIF investments.
Increasing the management fee from 2% to 3% to compensate for the extended tenure.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7 directly states: 'The investment managers have to understand the industry and market cycles, their own investment horizon, exit strategy and appropriately harvest returns... Since AIF is a long term investment strategy associated with illiquidity, harvesting returns by managing exit risks is probably the most important skill attribute of an investment manager.' Harvest phase is about exits and distributions, not fresh deployment or fee changes. The Trap: Option A confuses fundraising with harvesting. Option B ignores J-curve discipline (new deployment late in tenure is value-destructive). Option D is impermissible without LP consent and LPA amendment. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B tests exit-pathway awareness for distributors. XXI-B (PM) does NOT have a defined harvest phase — liquid portfolios turn over continuously. Manager's Pro-Tip: Start the exit-planning work in year 3, not year 6. IPO windows take 12-18 months of preparation, trade sales need 9-12 months of banker-led processes, and secondary sales to other PE/VC funds can take 6-9 months.
